Theme

School & learning

mood noun

in grammar

also moods, grammatical mood, what mood is it?, imperative mood, indicative mood, subjunctive mood

classical

Quint. 1.5.41: fīunt soloecismī per genera, tempora, persōnās, modōs
Traupman 225, 247

modus, modī m.

noun, second declension

a mood of the verb; in Quintilian also a voice

The question is Cujus modī est?, in what mood is it? (Traupman 240). Quintilian also calls the passive patiendī modus (9.3.7). The Roman grammarians counted five moods (indicative, subjunctive, imperative, infinitive, impersonal); modern grammars count three (Traupman 225).

Examples

  • ideōque in eō fīunt soloecismī per genera, tempora, persōnās, modōs

    and so in the verb mistakes happen in voice, tense, person and moodQuint. 1.5.41

  • Cujus modī est? — Indicātīvī.

    In what mood is it? — The indicative.Traupman 240

  • Modī quot sunt?

    How many moods are there?Traupman 225

  • modus imperātīvus, ut “lege!”

    the imperative mood, e.g. “read!”Traupman 347

  • modus indicātīvus, ut “legō”

    the indicative mood, e.g. “I read”Traupman 347

  • modus subjūnctīvus, ut “cum legam”

    the subjunctive mood, e.g. “although I read”Traupman 347

See also indicative, subjunctive, imperative, infinitive, verb, tense.
